forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

essentials.title: PROGRESS OF ACTION IDENTIFIED IN THE ANNUAL GOVERNANCE STATEMENT 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: South Derbyshire's audit team faces staffing pressures with recommendations from 2021/22 unresolved
news_drafts.lead: South Derbyshire Council's internal audit team is managing staffing pressure by using external associates to fill gaps, rather than more costly agency staff. Onboarding these associates has proved lengthy, with the council facing challenges around gaining system access for the new team members. Eight audits were completed this year with 24 recommendations made. Yet audit recommendations from 2021/22 remain unresolved, with the internal auditor referring to moderate and low-risk issues with the council's controls and procedures from these earlier audits still being outstanding. These represent actions, the auditor confirmed, that management continues to work on.

findings.headline: Housing has no survey of asbestos in kitchen tiles, which were removed only when a kitchen was due replacement
findings.detail: The Head of Housing said kitchen tiles containing asbestos were removed only where a house was due a kitchen replacement. The Council has no survey specifically recording these tiles across the stock, in response to a question from a Councillor.
findings.matters: An unsurveyed asbestos exposure across a housing stock is an unquantified liability a finance director would want to know about when assessing future remedial costs.
findings.quote: there was not a survey which specifically informed the Council on this matter

findings.headline: Twelve schools have affiliated to the Active Education Foundation, which is expected to bring funding into the organisation
findings.detail: The Head of Cultural and Community Services said twelve schools had affiliated and that this was due to bring funding in. The Coordinator contacted all schools in the district to secure them, and the organisation is being developed as a business development piece to retain and attract schools.
findings.matters: Affiliation income for a spun-out service is a new revenue stream that determines whether the transferred service is self-funding, which other councils considering similar transfers will want to know.
findings.figures: Twelve schools affiliated. No funding amount stated.
findings.quote: twelve schools had affiliated, which was due to bring funding into the organisation.

findings.headline: The Council committed to ceasing hosting of the South Derbyshire Active Schools Partnership from 31 December 2026
findings.detail: The Committee noted progress in transferring the function to the Active Education Foundation, recommended to Council that the Foundation be added to Outside Bodies with a Member as Trustee, and approved the termination of hosting from the date given. The minutes state that a separate exempt item covered staff, assets and a reserve budget transfer, and that its recommendations were approved.
findings.matters: An exit from hosting a service with a set end date, alongside a reserve budget transfer, is the kind of service transfer finance officers at other councils can use to compare their own arrangements.
findings.figures: Hosting ends 31 December 2026. Reserve transfer amount is in exempt material and not stated.
findings.quote: approved the termination of hosting the South Derbyshire Active Schools Partnership

findings.headline: An audit of all properties for damp and mould is to be completed by September 2027
findings.detail: The Head of Housing said the team used different reporting methods this year, so damp and mould figures cannot be compared with 2024-2025. In the meantime, residents are being educated on damp and mould and on when to report it.
findings.matters: A stock-wide audit with a fixed completion date is a deadline a finance director would track, since its results may bring remedial works costs that are not yet quantified.
findings.figures: Audit deadline: September 2027. No figures for damp and mould cases stated.
findings.quote: An audit of all properties was to be completed by September 2027

findings.headline: The Waites contract is extended a further two years to end in June 2028, with a review then
findings.detail: The Head of Housing said a two-year contract signed with Waites in June 2024 is to be extended for a further two years. At that point the contract is to be reviewed and other options explored. The Deputy Monitoring Officer confirmed the extension was agreed within the contract's terms, and a Councillor noted no update had gone to Overview and Scrutiny.
findings.matters: A contract extension running to 2028 fixes a commitment for a further two years and sets a review date that other councils planning similar contracts will want to compare.
findings.figures: Two-year original contract from June 2024; extension of a further two years to end in June 2028.
findings.quote: this was to be extended a further two years to end in June 2028
